Assess whether the following source-frozen institutional design intrinsically motivates an EVM smart-contract-account substrate, independent of regulatory compliance. Union law: each package/node is a sovereign settlement membrane owning its own law/classes, records, capabilities, books, offices, obligations, admissions and contracts; no ambient root pool exists. Durable acts are node-local append-only evidence. Every ingress and egress crosses the owning settlement's explicit boundary; another settlement may request but never write the target's plate. An enterprise is the territory over which gluing is enforced, while the market is where sovereign sections may disagree; prices, contracts, receipts and arbitration live on borders. A2A coordinates inside an enterprise; ActivityPub is the inter-enterprise message face; EAVT/Datom is the monotone source log; x402 receipts settle real priced boundary crossings. The sovereignty test is whether a settlement can operate, refuse, transact, attest, amend and improve with its inducer absent. A settlement possesses identity, constitution, books, authority, admissions, capabilities, borders, request channels and refusal. EVM smart-contract accounts provide globally addressable principals, code-defined authorization, signature validation, signer rotation/delegation, asset custody, calls, event logs, atomic composability and programmable conditional settlement on a shared replicated state machine. Limits: an EVM address is not legal identity; public-chain storage can violate confidentiality/data minimization; smart contracts do not supply internal governance, semantic protocols, truthful attestations, dispute judgment, content custody or complete local books; gas, chain governance, bridges, finality and key recovery can create external dependencies. Explain the strongest structural fit, the category errors to avoid, whether every sovereign settlement should have its own smart-contract account, and a precise meaning of 'use EVM for our systems' that preserves local sovereignty and protocol pluralism. Do not discuss EU AI Act compliance and do not propose implementation steps.
